'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Panjshir conflict]]
***The [[Taliban]] repeats its claim of having captured all of [[Panjshir Province]], releasing footage of [[Taliban Security Force|Taliban militants]] in front of the [[Official residence|gubernatorial palace]] in [[Bazarak]], the capital of the province. The [[National Resistance Front of Afghanistan]] continues to deny the Taliban's claims. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/taliban-claim-control-panjshir-evacuation-flights-await-clearance-2021-09-06/ (Reuters)]
***[[National Resistance Front of Afghanistan|Anti-Taliban forces]] in [[Panjshir Valley|Panjshir]] claim to have been bombed by [[Pakistan Air Force]] [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]], accusing [[Pakistan]] of directly supporting the [[2021 Taliban offensive|Taliban offensive]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/videos/world-news/panjshir-pakistan-air-force-dropped-bombs-via-drones-to-help-taliban-say-reports-afghanistan-101630909614845.html (''The Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[War crimes in the Tigray War]]
***In a single day, 11 more dead bodies of [[Tigrayans]] wash up along the [[Setit River]], most likely coming from [[Humera]]. According to refugees from Humera, Amhara militants have rounded up thousands of Tigrayans and forced them into makeshift mass detention camps while those of other ethnicities were safe, particularly those of the Amhara ethnicity. Inside these detention camps, people were crammed together on the floor without rooms or partitions to create privacy. These people were also not given food and sometimes did not even have access to a toilet. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/09/05/africa/ethiopia-tigray-humera-sudan-bodies-cmd-intl/index.html?utm_medium=social&utm_content=2021-09-06T18%3A15%3A06&utm_source=twCNNi&utm_term=link (CNN)]
*[[2021 Guinean coup d'état]]
**The [[military junta]] led by [[Colonel]] [[Mamady Doumbouya]] announces an indefinite nightly [[curfew]] in the country, and says that [[Guinea]]'s governors will be replaced by regional commanders of the [[Republic of Guinea Armed Forces|military]]. The junta also refuses to issue a timeline for the release of deposed [[List of presidents of Guinea|President]] [[Alpha Condé]], saying that the former leader still has "access to medical care and his doctors". [https://apnews.com/article/africa-guinea-d0426ca0b6fb0e40b3671a941e6d387e (AP)]
**Doumbouya announces the formation of a new government soon and says that there will be no "witch-hunting" of ministers or former ministers of the Condé government. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58461436 (BBC News)]
*Police in [[Algeria]] arrest 27 members of the separatist group [[Movement for the self-determination of Kabylie|MAK]], which has been blamed for two recent attacks in northern towns. The group is known for seeking independence for the Berber-speaking region of [[Kabylie]]. Algeria cited [[Morocco]]'s support for the group as a reason for suspending diplomatic relations last week. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/algeria-arrests-members-mak-separatist-group-after-attacks-2021-09-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[List of mayors of Mexico City|Mexico City Mayor]] [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] announces that the historic [[Monument to Christopher Columbus (Paseo de la Reforma)|Monument to Christopher Columbus]] in [[Paseo de la Reforma]] will be permanently replaced by a statue of a woman from the indigenous [[Olmecs|Olmec civilization]]. Sheinbaum says that the move is not an attempt to "erase history" but to instead deliver "[[social justice]]". The Columbus statue is reportedly being moved to a small park in the [[Polanco, Mexico City|Polanco]] neighborhood. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-58462071 (BBC News)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2021/09/06/mexico-city-removes-christopher-columbus-statue-indigenous-women/5748790001/ (USA Today)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The government of Colombia, through the [[Superintendency of Corporations]], ceases its control of the petrochemical firm ''Monómeros S.A.'' that had been under the management of the Venezuelan transitional government. This intervention takes place one week after Venezuelan President [[Nicolás Maduro]] called for the opposition to return control of the enterprise to Venezuela. [https://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/atencion-supersociedades-toma-el-control-de-la-empresa-monomeros-pretendida-por-nicolas-maduro/202150/ (''Semana'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 17 people are killed at a hospital during heavy [[flood]]s in [[Tula, Hidalgo]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58482986 (BBC News)] [https://www.milenio.com/estados/hospital-imss-tula-hidalgo-esto-sabemos-de-la-inundacion (''Milenio'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****[[India]] administers 10,576,296 doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in the past 24 hours, setting a new record for the third time in the past 11 days. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-sets-new-record-administers-over-1-crore-jabs-thrice-in-11-days-101630946589639.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
****An industry executive says that [[India]] will increase its medical oxygen capacity to 15,000 tonnes in preparation for a third wave of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-plans-50-increase-oxygen-production-before-third-covid-19-wave-2021-09-06/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports a record 22,415 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,103,331. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/news/nation/802255/philippines-registers-all-time-high-22-415-new-covid-19-cases/story/ (GMA News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]]ese authorities launch a plan to conduct [[COVID-19 testing]] of up to 1.5 million people in higher-risk areas of [[Hanoi]] in order to contain an outbreak of COVID-19 infections as the capital extends its COVID-19-related restrictions for two more weeks. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/vietnam-hanoi-covid-19-curbs-extend-2159056 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Denmark]]
****The [[Denmark|Danish]] [[Government of Denmark|governmment]] cancels its plans for a national vaccine production tender after they agreed to support [[Bavarian Nordic]]'s vaccine development with financial aid of [[Danish Krone|DKK]] 800 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]128 million). [https://m.medwatch.com/News/Pharma___Biotech/article13256979.ece (Medwatch)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kosovo]]
****[[Kosovo]] receives a shipment of 503,100 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] donated from the [[United States]] through the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.gazetaexpress.com/us-donation-of-vaccine-doses-will-allow-kosovo-to-protect-its-citizens-faster/ (Gazeta Express)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] begins to require a negative [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] [[COVID-19 testing|test result]] from the previous 48 hours for those who have not been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Turkey|fully vaccinated]] or who have not recovered from COVID-19 in order to enter theatres, cinemas, or other crowded events as well as to travel by plane, train or bus. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/turkey-launches-covid-19-test-scheme-for-the-unvaccinated/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Peru]]
*****[[President of Peru|Peruvian President]] [[Pedro Castillo]] announces that the Peruvian government has reached an agreement with [[Russia]] to create a plant that would produce a [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V vaccine]] in [[Peru|the country]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-build-plant-make-sputnik-v-covid-19-vaccine-president-2021-09-07/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
****The [[Public Health Institute of Chile]] approves the usage of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[vaccine]] for children over the age of six. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-06/chile-approves-sinovac-vaccine-for-children-as-young-as-six (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Kathy Hochul]] signs the HERO Act, a legislation that would provide protection to state workers in their workplaces. [https://www.nydailynews.com/news/politics/new-york-elections-government/ny-hochul-hero-act-covid-safety-rules-20210906-onjtp2vpjvbx7jzcq6hj7jf5gq-story.html (''New York Daily News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Germany–Russia relations]]
**The [[Germany|German]] government calls on [[Russia]] to cease its cyber-attack operations, alleging [[phishing]] attacks against members of the [[Bundestag]]. Those accused are believed to be "cyber-actors of the Russian state" and specifically from the [[GRU (Russian Federation)|GRU]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/germany-russia-cyber-attack/2021/09/06/7b9ca734-0f28-11ec-baca-86b144fc8a2d_story.html?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=wp_homepage (''Washington Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 Belarusian protests]]
**A court in [[Minsk]], [[Belarus]], finds [[Coordination Council (Belarus)|opposition activist]] [[Maria Kalesnikava]] guilty of "trying to seize power and extremism" and sentences her to 11 years in prison. Kalesnikava had destroyed [[Belarusian passport|her passport]] to avoid being expelled from the country. Opposition leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] promises to release Kalesnikava "much earlier than these 11 years" and condemns the verdict. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-protest-leader-kolesnikova-sentenced-11-years-jail-2021-09-06/ (Reuters)]
